questions.title: Who will score Bangladesh's first men's Test century on Australian soil?
questions.background: A Test century is an individual score of at least 100 runs in a single innings. No Bangladesh batter has yet achieved this milestone in a men's Test played in Australia.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Test match scorecards and contemporaneous reputable cricket reporting confirming the first such century. Resolution Condition : The question resolves when a player representing Bangladesh first reaches 100 runs in a single innings of an official men's Test match played in Australia. Accepted Answer Format : The batter's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-12 match-eve update ahead of Test 1 in Darwin starting Thursday Aug 13 (cricket.com.au, AP News, Reuters/Straits Times/Sportstar, BSS/tbsnews.net, Lokmat Times): Three material shifts reshape Bangladesh's century probabilities: (1) Litton Das (0.180 -> 0.205, now #1) was officially declared '100 per cent fit' by captain Shanto after Marrara batting/keeping drills and will play at #5 or #6, eliminating residual calf-injury discount; he is Bangladesh's leading Test scorer over the past 5 years (6 hundreds, avg 41.70, fresh off 126 & 69 vs Pakistan in June) and slots past the hardest new-ball phase. (2) Conflicting fitness signal on 39yo Mushfiqur Rahim (0.195 -> 0.140, down to #3): AP News (Aug 12) explicitly reported veteran Mushfiqur Rahim is 'ruled out due to a finger injury', whereas cricket.com.au (two Aug 12 articles, which updated the 1st-Test squad to add Litton and omit Nahid Rana/Shoriful Islam), Reuters, BSS (Aug 12 8:55 pm), and Aug 11 ABC News all keep Mushfiqur in the squad with zero mention of injury (and AP also oddly listed non-Test quick Mustafizur Rahman as unavailable). Assigning a Bayesian ~20-25% risk that AP caught a genuine Test-1/series finger knock, combined with Australia locking in their full-strength 'Fab Four' (Hazlewood edging Boland to reunite Cummins/Starc/Hazlewood/Lyon on a grassy drop-in pitch after Bangladesh's 54 all-out warm-up collapse — raising the ~25-30% chance no century occurs in 2026, where 39yo Mushfiqur has virtually zero future-tour share), drops Mushfiqur sharply while nudging up prime-age locked starters Najmul Hossain Shanto (#4 captain, 0.185 -> 0.195), Mominul Haque (#3 specialist, 0.125 -> 0.130), and Mehidy Hasan Miraz (#7 vice-captain who hit 109* at Marrara last week and is confirmed in the twin-spin attack, 0.115 -> 0.125). Top-5 sum = 0.795, preserving 0.205 outside for opener Shadman Islam (~0.090), Jaker Ali (~0.040, boosted as #6 replacement if Mushfiqur misses), Soumya Sarkar (~0.030), Tanzid Hasan Tamim (~0.025), and future-tour tail (~0.020).

local_articles.title: Lionel Messi returns after father’s death but Inter Miami knocked out of Leagues Cup

questions.title: Who will win the women's 50m freestyle at the 2026 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official championship results published by the organizers or World Aquatics, corroborated by contemporaneous sports reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the swimmer awarded the gold medal in the women's 50m freestyle at the 2026 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships, once the final result is announced. Accepted Answer Format : The swimmer's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major Aug 12 Pan Pacific Championships Day 1 prelims evidence (Swimming World, SwimSwam, NBC Sports Aug 10, Yahoo Sports Aug 12) drives a sharp upward revision for Kate Douglass (+0.12 to 0.28) and downward cuts for Torri Huske (-0.06 to 0.03) and Meg Harris (-0.04 to 0.11). In this morning's Day 1 Women's 50m butterfly prelims in Irvine, Kate Douglass became only the third woman in history under 25 seconds (24.99 meet record) before Gretchen Walsh answered one heat later in 24.91, while Torri Huske swam a sluggish 26.19 (7th overall, knocked out of the A final by Walsh and Douglass under the 2-per-country cap). Moreover, NBC Sports, Yahoo Sports, and SwimSwam previews all project the 23.55 WR holder Walsh vs 23.59 #2 all-time Douglass head-to-head in Saturday's 50m free (with SwimSwam's Aug 10 preview listing Douglass's core schedule as 50/100 free, 100/200 breast, 50 fly—omitting 200 IM), lowering Douglass's Day 4 scratch risk from ~45-50% to ~25% (a Saturday double with her Olympic gold event 200m breast still poses modest scratch risk). Combining ~75% probability Douglass swims (where Walsh ~51%, Douglass ~39%, Harris ~8%, and all other Americans are nearly locked out of the A final) with ~25% probability Douglass scratches (Walsh ~70%, Harris ~18%, Huske ~8%, Manuel ~2%) yields Gretchen Walsh 0.55, Kate Douglass 0.28, Meg Harris 0.11, Torri Huske 0.03, and Simone Manuel 0.01 (sum 0.98, 0.02 residual).

local_articles.title: France’s Florent Manaudou, Olympic 50m freestyle champion, retires at 35
local_articles.snippet: PARIS - French swimmer Florent Manaudou, the 2012 Olympic champion in 50m freestyle, announced he would bid farewell to the sport on Aug 15 at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris. “Two years later, I’m announcing the end,” the 35-year-old told France TV on Aug 13, referring to the fact he has not competed since the 2024 Paris Games, where he claimed bronze in his signature event. Manaudou, one of France’s greatest swimmers, departs with six Olympic medals. As well as the gold in 2012, he captured three silvers and two bronzes across appearances at four Games. The younger brother of Laure, 2004 Olympic champion, also bagged multiple World Championship titles. REUTERS
